observations.why: The 'we' enacts communal-sharing — the team as an undifferentiated body that shipped together, not an individual reporting personal output.

payload.rationale: This document is a later sprint retro (2026-08-25) that echoes the prior Sprint 4 retro (2026-03-22) almost verbatim — same 23-point velocity claim, same Zephyr-as-key-unlock framing, same async decision widget. I expanded the prior retro sample, the Zephyr integration position, the velocity observation, the thesis-proven position, and the metric-anchor style observation so the passes can determine whether this is a duplicate, an update, or a new observation. I also surfaced the DecisionCaptureAtConsensus and AntiSlackPositioning narratives (plus the anti-pattern and product-category positions under the latter) because the async decision widget is the product embodiment of those narratives, and the passes need them to place or evolve the document's themes. I deliberately did NOT expand Position_PricingTwelveDollars or Position_TargetMarketRemoteTeams — this document touches neither pricing nor segmentation.

positions.name: Sprint4SuccessEvidenceMarshaling
positions.frame: what evidence does this retrospective marshal to establish that the sprint succeeded?
positions.why: The three assertions are not independent facts but a stacked evidentiary sequence: a completed deliverable (shipped), a quantified performance superlative (23 points, highest this quarter), and a causal attribution naming the enabling factor (Zephyr integration). All three sit at claim-level conviction (unhedged but unratified) and past/realis/concrete temporal footing, and the value reads (competence, self-enhancement) run consistently across them — together they build the case for sprint success rather than each standing as a freestanding report. There is a register shift worth holding in tension: src-1 carries activated-positive energy ('We shipped') while src-2 and src-3 settle into calm-positive, measured retrospective evaluation — the announcement cools into evidence.

placements.why: All three assertions evidence the practical realization of the capture-at-consensus thesis rather than opening a new theme: the shipped widget (src-1) is the artifact that performs consensus-moment capture; the record velocity (src-2) is Tina's own attributed proof that the capture mechanism works without friction; and the Zephyr integration (src-3) is the infrastructure that delivers the leaf's own stated 'zero extra steps' property by embedding capture directly in existing chat surfaces. This matches the leaf's description verbatim ('captures the decision at the moment it's made and links it to the producing context — zero extra steps') rather than introducing a new subject: these are proof points feeding an existing theme, not a fact standing alone (grain test). Anti-Slack positioning and the decisions-evaporate problem framing were considered but are not what these segments are about — they report the solution working, not the market frame or the pain point.
